question: Who among the following was one of the “Lal-Bal-Pal” of the freedom movement of India?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Lala Lajpat Rai.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai of Punjab, Bal Gangadhar Tilak of Maharashtra, and Bipin Chandra Pal of Bengal were popularly known as Lal Bal Pal**.
 
• They advocated the Swadeshi movement involving the boycott of all imported items and the use of Indian-made goods in 1907 during the anti-Partition **agitation in Bengal which began in 1905.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• ** Lala Lajpat Rai**

 
 
• ​Born in undivided **Punjab on 28 January 1865.**
 
• In 1895, he started the Punjab National Bank—the first Indian bank to begin solely with the Indian capital.
 
• He focused his efforts on a self-sufficient India.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**
 
 
• Tilak was a loud voice against the British rule.
 
• His articles in newspapers like Kesari, which he founded in 1881 had earned him strong support from like-minded people like the Chapekar brothers.
 
• **With the slogan “Swarajya majha janmasiddha hakka ahe… Ani to me milavnarach,**” he ignited strong patriotism among his Marathi peers. “Swarajya (self-rule) is my birthright, and I shall have it” became a popular chant during the freedom struggle.
 
• Tilak was the “Father of the Indian Unrest.” according to Britishers.
 
 
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal** ​
 
 
• The father of revolutionary thoughts, Bipin Chandra Pal, was born to a wealthy family in Sylhet, Bengal Presidency (now in Bangladesh).
 
• Pal was a journalist by profession and had always turned to his pen to unite efforts of Indians for Swarajya and Swadeshi goods.
